title: Structured Output Validator
summary: Build a tool that validates and repairs raw model output against a JSON schema: strips markdown fences, fixes trailing commas, reports what it couldn't fix.
requirements: Accept raw model output text and a target JSON schema (required fields at minimum).
Strip markdown code fences if present.
Parse the repaired text as JSON.
Validate the parsed object against the schema, reporting the SPECIFIC missing/wrong-typed field.
start: Start from Module 1's exercise function signature and generalize it: accept an arbitrary schema object instead of a hardcoded one, so the same validator works across different response shapes.
acceptance: A response wrapped in a markdown fence is correctly repaired and validated.
A response with a trailing comma is correctly repaired and validated.
A response missing a required field is rejected with that field named specifically, not a generic error.
Prose with no JSON structure at all is rejected gracefully, never raises uncaught.
A wrong-typed field (string where number expected) is caught and reported.
tests: Clean, valid JSON matching schema → passes.
Trailing comma before closing brace → repaired and passes.
Missing required field → fails, names the field.
Pure prose, no JSON at all → fails gracefully, no exception escapes.
mistakes: Stripping the trailing comma AFTER attempting json.loads() instead of before.
A generic 'validation failed' error instead of naming the specific field.
Letting a json.loads() exception propagate uncaught instead of catching and returning a structured failure.
solution: Strip a leading/trailing markdown fence via regex.
Strip trailing commas before `}`/`]` via regex.
Walk the schema's required fields, checking presence and type, collecting every violation, not just the first.
